analysis.title: Chip rout tests AI investment case (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: US tech led markets lower Thursday as the post-election relief rally reversed on concern about how Democratic gains, especially at state level, affect AI infrastructure and data centers. Nasdaq 100 fell about 6.4% and S&P 500 about 4.4%.
Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.3%, extending its drawdown since June to around 38.3%. Qualcomm fell sharply after its profit outlook disappointed.
Selling extended into Friday in Asia: Nikkei 225 down around 6%, Kospi down 5.5%, Taiwan's benchmark down 4.7% at the time of writing.
Investors are focusing on how congressional oversight and state government changes could affect electricity consumption, water use, permitting and development costs for data centers.

UBS reads the decline as uncertainty about the cost and pace of the data center buildout and a de-risking event, not a material change in fundamentals. Investors are shifting from rewarding spending commitments to demanding evidence of monetization, capacity utilization, returns and ability to raise capital.

UBS expects the election result to keep tech volatility elevated. Broad federal restrictions are unlikely except after a widespread AI security issue, and state and local decisions will more likely decide where projects are built, their cost and their timing.

Proposed US data center capacity of about 400 GW far exceeds UBS's buildout assumption of roughly 90 GW by 2030. Regulation may redistribute and extend the investment cycle rather than derail it, with power access, permitting, financing and execution separating winners from losers.

UBS forecasts aggregate AI capital spending of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. Recent earnings showed accelerating cloud revenue and growing advance orders for compute, and reports point to significant chip backlogs among Chinese buyers.

UBS would see a lasting AI downturn if AI revenue growth slowed, cloud utilization weakened, lower AI costs failed to generate enough new usage, algorithmic efficiency sharply cut compute needs, bigger investments failed to produce gains in capability, or tighter financial conditions constrained spending by the largest platforms and labs.

Breadth is the near-term signal. Weakness concentrated in chips, data centers and highly valued growth stocks fits a valuation and positioning adjustment. A sustained spread into financials, industrials and cyclicals, especially with weaker economic, credit or earnings data, would signal a broader reassessment. UBS says current evidence does not support that.
UBS sees upside in broad equity indices over six to 12 months and calls the sell-off overdone. It would use volatility to add diversified exposure to higher-quality companies.

Portfolio advice: reduce excessive single-stock concentration versus tech and broad benchmarks. Within AI, favor financially strong platform and application companies and infrastructure companies with pricing power, diversified across foundry, compute and power.

Sector and regional stance: US IT cut to Neutral in February, and US Communication Services also cut to Neutral. Preferred sectors are industrials, health care and financials. Regionally preferred: Eurozone, emerging markets and Asia ex-Japan. Investors overweight US tech should consider rebalancing.

Fixed income: investors with large bond underweights should consider rebuilding strategic allocations, favoring high-quality short- to medium-maturity bonds and EM bonds. UBS is cautious on the longest maturities because of fiscal deficits and heavy issuance.

Germany's fiscal expansion is showing up in defense, construction and labor demand. The federal deficit widened to EUR 64.2bn in the quarter to September, about two-thirds of the annual target. Federal investment slowed in Q3. UBS forecasts German GDP growth rising from 1.0% in 2026 to 1.5% in 2027, supports German equities, and expects little impact on Bund yields from higher issuance.
Market backdrop: Brent rebounded to around USD 100 per barrel, 10-year Treasury yield fell 5bp to near 4.84%, gold holding near USD 4,042/oz.

trade_ideas.description: Use the volatility to add diversified exposure to higher-quality AI companies (platform, application and infrastructure names with pricing power) and rebalance overweight US tech toward industrials, health care, financials, the Eurozone, EM and Asia ex-Japan.
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS says the sell-off is overdone and the AI investment cycle remains intact.
trade_ideas.risk: Greater clarity on data center policy may be needed before volatility fades.

trade_ideas.description: Rebuild strategic bond exposure in high-quality short- to medium-maturity bonds and EM bonds.
trade_ideas.rationale: Diversification and income ahead of potential further equity volatility.
trade_ideas.risk: Persistent fiscal deficits and heavy issuance, which make UBS cautious on the longest maturities.

risk_factors: Data center policy uncertainty from congressional oversight and state and local decisions on power, water, permitting and costs.
Slowing AI revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, or lower AI costs failing to create enough new usage.
Algorithmic efficiency gains that sharply cut compute demand, or larger investments failing to deliver commensurate AI capability gains.
Tighter financial conditions constraining spending by the largest tech platforms and frontier labs.
Selling spreading into financials, industrials and cyclicals alongside weaker economic, credit or earnings data.
A widespread AI security issue, which could prompt broad federal restrictions.
Oil near USD 100 and geopolitical developments.
Persistent fiscal deficits and heavy issuance weighing on long-dated bonds.
German implementation bottlenecks, capacity constraints, skills mismatches and supply-chain issues.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility is more elevated at the individual stock level than in broad indices. UBS advises reducing excessive single-stock concentration versus tech and broad benchmarks.
High expectations and concentrated positions have increased the sensitivity of AI-linked stocks to guidance, regulation and risk appetite.
UBS expects tech volatility to stay elevated after the election. Structured strategies may help manage downside or generate income, with issuer, liquidity, pricing and capital-loss risks.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index drawdown since June is about 38.3%.
geopolitical: US midterm election result: Democratic gains, especially at state level, raise questions about data center and AI regulation and greater congressional oversight.
Oil and geopolitical developments remain a secondary source of volatility, with Brent back near USD 100.
Recent reports point to significant chip backlogs among Chinese buyers.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says AI demand is strong: accelerating cloud revenue, growing advance orders for compute, Chinese chip backlogs, and proposed US capacity of about 400 GW versus its 90 GW assumption. Regulation would redistribute and extend the cycle rather than derail it.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors are demanding evidence of monetization and returns. State and local policy, congressional oversight, power and water constraints and permitting could raise costs and delay projects. Concentrated positions make AI stocks sensitive to guidance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowing AI revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, selling spreading into financials, industrials and cyclicals with weaker economic, credit or earnings data, or algorithmic efficiency gains that sharply cut compute needs.

theme_stances.key_argument: The decline reflects uncertainty about data center cost and pace, not a deterioration in the outlook, and looks like a de-risking event.
theme_stances.evidence: the decline reflects uncertainty about the cost and pace of the data center buildout

theme_stances.key_argument: Federal restrictions face legislative and presidential constraints, while state and local decisions will decide where, how fast and at what cost projects are built.
theme_stances.evidence: State and local decisions are more likely to determine where projects are built

theme_stances.key_argument: Fiscal expansion should increasingly lift growth through year-end and into 2027, supporting German equities.
theme_stances.evidence: Germany's fiscal expansion should provide an increasingly visible boost to economic growth
